scope: Presentation-only expiry/lock audit of complete picks and the leaderboard. No collected quote, probability, roster, pick engine or source evidence is rewritten.

sources.method: Read the official rendered page through fetch_page. This session did not capture the original HTTP bytes.
sources.excerpt: Picks lock 5 minutes before the scheduled start time, so make sure you submit before the countdown reaches zero.
sources.limitation: The existing fixture API separately supplies a six-minute offset. This change uses only explicit saved locks_at values and never infers a deadline from either statement.

sources.method: Line-by-line code review plus synthetic regression tests.
sources.finding: The old complete-picks renderer printed green Pick/checkbox cues irrespective of current lock or line age. Corrected in the server renderer and a shared browser guard.

sources.method: Line-by-line code review plus pinned-clock browser tests.
sources.finding: The old runtime only hid locked cards. Current-use expiry now retires the verdict, score-submit advice, shortlist links, aggregate synopsis and count as inventory/quotes age.

verification.note: Synthetic fixtures are served from an OS temporary directory and are never written to published data or the Pages artifact. Automated axe coverage is not complete WCAG certification.

limitations: A browser device clock is not independently authenticated. Future/unparseable times fail closed; a retired recommendation cannot be revived merely by rolling the clock back.
With JavaScript disabled, the page is checked at build time only. A visible no-JS warning says to compare printed deadlines and quote times before relying on it.

Browser timers can pause in background tabs. Guards recheck every 30 seconds and on focus, pageshow and visibility restoration, but do not claim server-side submission or guaranteed wall-clock enforcement.
Historical numbers remain published as historical estimates with original sources; they are not new betting lines or guaranteed true win chances.

follow_up.finding: A no-upset fallback instruction also needs expiry protection; a multi-day aggregate must not say today.
follow_up.handling: Added the same synopsis retirement guard to the no-upset favorite callout; label the total across listed fixtures and explicitly state the cap is per UTC day. No probability or rule threshold changed.

verification.synthetic_cases: No-upset favorite callout starts usable and becomes hidden after inventory/line expiry, with probabilities retained. Seven synthetic layouts now audited at four widths and axe at phone/desktop.

edge_guards: Partial initial deadline coverage must not produce an all-fixtures favorite instruction.

The no-JS current-upset count and shortlist use canonical presentation eligibility, even if inherited strategy eligibility tolerates an extra minute of future clock skew. The underlying strategy decision is retained as history.
